invariant.when: A user action, command option, host event, or scheduled boundary is documented or configured to trigger behavior through an execution path.
invariant.require: The real trigger must traverse its dispatch path to the responsible implementation and produce the intended durable or domain effect.
invariant.verify: Exercise the trigger through its actual boundary and observe the downstream effect rather than accepting parsing, registration, scheduling, or local presentation as proof of execution.

preservedDomainDetails.detail: Reload the browser and confirm the durable preference value so cosmetic local state cannot satisfy acceptance.
Confirm that the generated artifact contains the records selected by the requested export scope.
Emit the event through the host dispatcher instead of directly invoking the registered handler.
Advance the test clock through the scheduler boundary and confirm that expired records are removed.

counterexamples: rule-web-keyboard-access and proposal 2026-07-09-web-keyboard-access concern input accessibility: focus, semantic role, and keyboard equivalence can fail even when dispatch and durable execution work correctly.

rule-hook-retry-idempotency and proposal 2026-07-10-hook-retry-idempotency concern duplicate side effects across retries: the handler may execute successfully while still producing the effect more than once.
behaviorLostIfApproved: No verified acceptance guarantee is intentionally removed: the four surface-specific execution rules become one shared dispatch-to-effect invariant, while their browser reload, export-scope content, host-dispatcher, and scheduler-clock checks remain explicit domain details. The lost content is only repeated surface-specific phrasing.
